text.p: These are the leading stories in Malawi's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former Secretary General of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) Bingu Mutharika announced on Friday from Lilongwe, that he had formed Malawi's 16th political party, the United Party (UP).
- At least 10 police officers are on interdiction and others serving prison sentences for various crimes, as a cleaning up exercise in the police force to strengthen its public confidence continues.

- Seven men claiming to be President Bakili Muluzi's bodyguards during the 1994 general elections on Friday refused to enter the magistrate's court after they were detained overnight at the Blantyre police station.
- Two sisters were on Friday burnt to death in their bedroom, in Blantyre after a candle kindled a fierce fire while they slept during the evening during an electricity black-out.
- Police on Friday arrested a Blantyre business tycoon, Kwacha Ghambi, in an operation they code-named "Operation Big Fish and Dangerous Drugs".
